newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria airline says traffic normal after strike.
newsitem.headline: Algeria airline says traffic normal after strike.

text.p: Algeria's state-owned airline Air Algerie said on Wednesday traffic was back to normal after a two-day strike by pilots.

"Air Algerie announces the normalisation of the conditions to carry out its programme for domestic and international traffic," said the Algerian national carrier in a statement reported by the official Algerian news agency APS.
Air Algerie's pilots staged strikes on Monday and Tuesday bringing traffic at Algiers airport to a near standstill.

They walked out to display solidarity with colleagues, on hunger strike, to protest against the dismissal of more than 50 pilots by the company after a strike last summer over pay and better working conditions.
Air Algerie board called the two-day strike illegal without mentioning any demands raised by the pilots.
It was not immediately known how many were continuing the hunger strike. Newspapers on Wednesday said two strikers had been taken to hospital.
